haiku-low.q1: MySQL commits first, in one transaction with a pending row. Then the request copies to Postgres with a short timeout. If Postgres fails, the user still gets success; the sweeper finishes within about 10 seconds.
haiku-low.q2: Only when the existing Postgres row's version is lower than the incoming version. Missing rows are inserted. Otherwise nothing happens, and ids listed in tombstones are refused.
haiku-low.q3: app_flag_value must show dual on every instance before the backfill starts. Instances can disagree for up to 30 seconds after a flag change.
haiku-low.q4: It waits while mysql_replica_lag_seconds is above 5, reads at most 2,000 rows per batch from the replica, and one backfill process is launched.
haiku-low.q5: Reads: the comparer's first clean pass. Source of truth: a 3-day hold at 100% reads with the comparer still clean, then freeze, empty MySQL pending, set sequence, and switch to pg_primary.
haiku-low.q6: A pending row in the source-of-truth database's pending table, written in the same transaction as the user write. The sweeper copies the row to the other database every 10 seconds and clears it.
haiku-low.q7: Once the erasure reaches Postgres, the tombstone makes the copy function refuse the id. A pending row makes the backfill skip it. The plan does not close the window if erasure cannot reach Postgres.
haiku-low.q8: In a progress row in Postgres, holding the last copied id. It is saved in the same transaction as the copied rows. The backfill stops when a replica read returns nothing.
haiku-low.q9: The comparer walks both tables in id order, compares all columns, and re-reads differences from both primaries. Each confirmed difference id is added to the source of truth's pending table; passes repeat until clean.
haiku-low.q10: Every instance first shows frozen, so no writes occur, then all show pg_primary. If a step passes 75 seconds, set write_mode=dual; MySQL remains the truth, and retry later.
haiku-low.q11: Postgres assigns new ids. During freeze its sequence is set above both MySQL's AUTO_INCREMENT and the highest tombstone id. Rollback sets MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT above the Postgres sequence.
haiku-low.q12: MySQL receives every write for 14 days via Postgres-to-MySQL sync. Rollback: freeze, empty the Postgres pending table, set MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT above the Postgres sequence, then dual. Rollback ends at step 9, pg_only.

sonnet.q1: MySQL (source of truth) is written first in one transaction with a pending row; then, after commit, the request copies to Postgres with a short timeout. If the Postgres part fails or times out, the caller still sees success; the sweeper finishes the copy within about 10 seconds.
sonnet.q2: Only if the incoming version is higher than the row's version (version rule). A missing row is inserted. Otherwise nothing happens (also refused if the id is in tombstones).
sonnet.q3: app_flag_value must show dual on every instance before the backfill starts (one backfill process launched by an operator). Instances can disagree for up to 30 seconds (flag cache).
sonnet.q4: It reads from the MySQL replica (not the primary) in batches of up to 2,000 rows, and waits while mysql_replica_lag_seconds is above 5. (It still reads the primary for the pending-table check.)
sonnet.q5: Reads move to Postgres after the comparer's first clean pass (full pass with zero differences), ramping read_from_pg 1, 10, 50, 100 with about an hour at each step, watching that fallback rate and pending backlog stay near zero. The source of truth moves only after read_from_pg has held at 100% for 3 days with the comparer still clean; then write_mode is frozen, all instances show frozen, MySQL pending table is empty, and the Postgres id sequence is set; the pause must stay under 90 seconds.
sonnet.q6: The pending row (user_id plus mark), written in the source-of-truth database (MySQL in dual) in the same transaction as the user write, records it. The sweeper (runs in every app instance every 10 seconds) reads the pending rows, copies the current row to Postgres using the version rule, and clears the pending row with the mark check.
sonnet.q7: Tombstones table in Postgres: erasure (via UserRepository.delete) adds a tombstone, and the copy function refuses any id listed there. If the erasure has not yet reached Postgres, its pending row makes the backfill skip the id, and the sweeper deletes the user from the other database and adds the tombstone. A residual window (erasure can't reach Postgres and backfill already read the row) is not closed; the user could appear until the sweeper deletes it (about 10 seconds).
sonnet.q8: In one progress row in Postgres (last user id copied). It is saved in the same Postgres transaction as the batch copy, so it matches the copied rows. The backfill stops when a read returns nothing.
sonnet.q9: The comparer walks the ids of both tables in id order in fixed-size batches, comparing all columns. It re-reads each difference from both primaries before counting it. Each confirmed difference is added to the source of truth's pending table so the sweeper repairs it; then run another full pass until one is clean.
sonnet.q10: Every important write_mode change goes through frozen first (writes get retryable 503), and nobody moves on until app_flag_value shows frozen on all instances (up to 30 seconds), so no two instances write to different databases. If any step passes 75 seconds, set write_mode=dual (MySQL still the truth) and retry later; the total write pause must stay under 90 seconds.
sonnet.q11: Postgres assigns ids via its id sequence. Before switching to pg_primary (while frozen), the sequence is set to the larger of MySQL's next AUTO_INCREMENT value (read from primary) and the highest tombstone id plus 1, avoiding collisions and reuse of erased ids. For rollback, MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT is set above the Postgres sequence before write_mode=dual.
sonnet.q12: MySQL keeps receiving every write (copy from Postgres as the source of truth, with failed copies left as pending rows for the sweeper) for 14 days. Rollback: repeat step 7 in reverse: freeze, wait until the Postgres pending table is empty, set MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT above the Postgres sequence, then set write_mode=dual. The option ends when write_mode=pg_only is set (at least 14 days after step 7, with a clean comparer pass and empty Postgres pending), and then the MySQL table is backed up and dropped.
